newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open slighty down on U.S. dip.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open slighty down on U.S. dip.

text.p: The Australian share market opened mixed to lower on Monday following overnight losses on Wall Street from Wednesday's record levels and as the Broken Hill Pty Co continued to lose ground.
By 10.15 a.m. (0015 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 4.3 points lower at 2,713.4 in turnover of A$73.30 million.
"BHP is the focus of everybody's attention with the media talk about management. It will probably dominate today's trade," said Richard Herring of Burrell & Co in Brisbane.

The stock fell another 16 cents to A$17.28 after sliding three percent on Thursday on concern about the conglomerate's costs and the direction of its mineral division following two resignations from senior ranks.
"It is starting to get down to the levels where it looks cheap, but with the board problems there is still concern out there," Richard Herring said.
Firmer metal prices and a stronger London listing helped global miner Rio Tinto gain 20 cents to A$21.05, while WMC was one cent lower at A$7.64.
Gold stocks were slighty higher on firmer bullion overnight.
Sector heavyweight Normandy Mining gained one cent to A$1.53, while Lihir Gold firmed two to A$1.87.

Coca-Cola Amatil came down a further 27.5 cents to A$15.90 as the market digested Wednesday's half-year results. Analysts said they had downgraded expectations for the bottler over concerns about returns from its European operations.

Trading in tobacco group W.D. & H.O. Wills resumed after Thursday's suspension in response to uncertainty over the replacement of state taxes with federal taxes. The stock gained two cents to A$2.02 in minimal turnover, while its competitor Rothmans Holdings was unchanged at A$7.85.

Manufacturer and investment group Austrim fell 10 cents to A$4.35 in active trade after it said it would not proceed to compulsory acquisition of the 12.22 percent stake in auto parts manufacturer Hawker still outstanding after the closure of Austrim's A$1.86 per share takeover offer.

Western Metals were steady at A$1.30 ahead of the lead and zinc producer's full-year results due later today, while casino and hotel operator Jupiters lost two cents to trade at A$3.32 despite showing a 21.9 percent increase in full-year net profits to A$41.29 million.

Transport and industrials services group Brambles lost 10.8 cents to a A$20 after hitting a record high on Thursday following the release of positive results from its partner in the Chep pallet business, GKN Plc.
Fashion retailer Country Road more than recovered Thursday's losses, triggered by a gloomy outlook on full-year profits, by rising 20 cents to A$1.60.
